record.final_answer:
No. I found no published number for Marrowlog over TLS, so nothing shows it will handle 50k lines/s.

**The closest published benchmark** is a note from an earlier session. It points to the Marrowlog 2.4 perf report for 2026 Q2 (marrowlog.example/perf/2026-q2, published 2026-06-18), which is the maintainers' own benchmark:
- One agent shipped **180,000 lines/s** on 1 vCPU and 2 GiB RAM, at 85% CPU (median of three 30-minute runs).
- **TLS was never turned on.** The test used plain TCP, lines of at most 200 bytes, the disk buffer off and `batch_lines: 500`.
- The report says outright that TLS, longer lines and the disk buffer were not measured. The maintainers plan to measure TLS in the Q4 report.

I checked for that Q4 report just now and it doesn't seem to be out yet: `/perf/2026-q4` returns 404.

**How that compares with your setup** (from `README.md` and `config/agent.yaml`):
- Same agent version (2.4), same 1 vCPU, same `batch_lines: 500`, disk buffer also off. That part matches.
- Your lines average about 900 bytes, roughly 4.5 times the benchmark's ceiling. At 50k lines/s that's about 45 MB/s per agent, compared with at most about 36 MB/s in the benchmark. So in bytes, you're already past what was measured, even before adding encryption.
- With TLS added, the 180k figure tells you little about your case.

My guess, which nothing published supports: 50k lines/s is under a third of the benchmark rate, so it may well be fine. But encrypting 45 MB/s on one core, already at 85% CPU on a lighter load, is the part nobody has measured. The safest step is to run our own test before the deadline: one agent, 1 vCPU, real ~900-byte JSON lines, `tls: true`, for 30 minutes at 50k lines/s, watching CPU use and queue backlog. Or wait for the Q4 report, if it arrives in time.
